synthesis.body: `shutil.copytree(src, dst)` defaults to `symlinks=False`, which means symlinks in `src` are DEREFERENCED — the link target's contents land in `dst`. Same for `shutil.copy2` (default `follow_symlinks=True`). When projecting source files that may be attacker-controlled (third-party packs, plugin submissions, untrusted catalogues) into a published output tree, a malicious symlink to `/etc/passwd` exfiltrates the build host's secrets into the artifact. Pass `symlinks=True` to copytree and `follow_symlinks=False` to copy2 — they preserve symlinks as symlinks rather than dereferencing. Caught by the security-reviewer pass on RFC-0001's distribution pipeline; not exploitable today (packs are repo-owned) but lethal the day production packs from PRs are admitted.

title: shutil.copytree follows symlinks by default — supply-chain hazard for published artifacts
